identity_scope: Digests identify the exact UTF-8 excerpts transcribed from public primary records in a web reader. The reader did not expose whole-publisher-response bytes or a version suffix for these abstract snapshots. Full-response digests and revision numbers are unknown. Publication dates denote first submission when an arXiv paper has revisions. Public read access conveys no hardware, commercial data, operating, or model rights.

sources.title: Towards Efficient Edge AI for Power Flow in Renewable-Rich Grids with Volt/VAR Control
sources.publisher: Puthanpurayil, Sanduleac and Teodorescu via arXiv
sources.excerpt: for edge inference on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano (15 W), solves an hourly scenario in 12.2 ms
sources.scope: One distilled model, one edge device and a modified IEEE 118-bus system; the number is for one hourly scenario.
sources.limitation: This latency alone cannot settle batched throughput across networks and solvers. Flat and warm Newton–Raphson baselines are also reported in section 4.3.

sources.title: Benchmarking CPU, GPU, and ML Power-Flow Solvers from 14 to 70,000 Buses
sources.publisher: Donnot, Tazi, Boguslawski and Henka via arXiv
sources.excerpt: a sufficiently parallelized CPU solver or gpusim2grid matches or exceeds the throughput of the ML surrogates we test
sources.scope: Comparative throughput on ordinary AC power flow. The authors tested nine physics-based methods and three ML surrogates across fifteen grid sizes.
sources.limitation: This finding is specific to the tested systems and ordinary power flow. Optimal power flow and local wall time involve other questions.
sources.earlier_condition: The seven CPU implementations in the study predated the comparison. Baseline choice materially changes the perceived speedup.

sources.title: CellTrack-Bench: Microscopic Cell Tracking Benchmark for Vision-Language Models
sources.publisher: Theodoro, Bragantini and Royer via arXiv
sources.locator: Abstract, construction of difficulty-selected set; appendix A.2
sources.excerpt: We selected a hard subset requiring greater reasoning effort by identifying failures shared across distinct algorithmic trackers.
sources.scope: Difficult associations were deliberately selected for overlapping algorithmic mistakes. The original full benchmark has 1,537 problems and 9,041 link decisions.
sources.limitation: Performance on the difficulty-selected rows is not an unbiased estimate for all links in a beneficiary's image sequence.
sources.earlier_condition: The public comparison builds on existing specialized trackers and annotated time-lapse datasets.
